title: Valid finite coefficient refinements form a directed set
statement:
The valid finite coefficient refinements occurring in
[def-nagata-noetherian-stage] are nonempty and directed under
inclusion. If $\lambda\leq\mu$, inclusion of coefficient algebras induces
compatible affine chart maps $S_\mu\to S_\lambda$; these maps satisfy the
identity and composition laws.

proof.text:
The selected valid stage is one object. Given two valid refinements, take
the union of their finite coefficient lists and then a common upper bound of
the finitely many stages witnessing their gluing equations. The finite-data
lemma makes the resulting refinement valid and above both inputs. Inclusion
of coefficient rings induces the affine maps on every chart. Their
restrictions agree on overlaps by the gluing equations, so they glue; the
identity and composition laws hold chartwise and therefore globally.

blueprint_update.statement:
The valid stages occurring in [def-nagata-noetherian-stage] are nonempty
and directed under inclusion: the chartwise sum
$(A_{\lambda,a}+A_{\mu,a})_a$ of the subrings of two valid stages
(the subring they generate) is again a valid stage, above both. If
$\lambda\leq\mu$, the inclusions $A_{\lambda,a}\subseteq A_{\mu,a}$ induce
compatible chart maps
$\operatorname{Spec}(A_{\mu,a})\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_{\lambda,a})$,
which glue to a transition morphism $S_\mu\to S_\lambda$; these morphisms
satisfy the identity and composition laws.

proof.text:
The selected valid stage $\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$ is one object. For two
valid stages, the generated subrings are finitely generated and contain the
basic-open elements; localization commutes with the generated subring, so
$(A_{\lambda,a}+A_{\mu,a})[1/f_{abr}]
=A_{\lambda,a}[1/f_{abr}]+A_{\mu,a}[1/f_{abr}]
=A_{\lambda,b}[1/g_{abr}]+A_{\mu,b}[1/g_{abr}]$, and the unit conditions
are inherited from either stage because the localizations only grow. Hence
the chartwise sum is valid and lies above both inputs.

Inclusion of coefficient rings induces the maps on every chart; they carry
the overlaps $\bigcup_rD(f_{abr})$ into each other and are compatible with
the overlap maps, which are determined by their compatibility with the maps
from $U_a\cap U_b$, so they glue. The identity and composition laws hold
chartwise and therefore globally.
